I don’t have direct access to VirusTotal’s live database from within this chat interface, so I can’t pull the exact list of URLs right now.  
What I *can* give you is a ready‑to‑run recipe (curl + Python) that will let you grab those URLs yourself, along with some tips on pagination and handling the `cursor` value you mentioned (`tr_cursor1`).  

---

### Quick Reference – How to Pull Up To 20 URLs From a Domain Search

| Step | What You Need | Example |
|------|---------------|---------|
| **API Key** | Your personal VT key (`tr_key001`) | `XVT_API_KEY=tr_key001` |
| **Endpoint** | `/domains/{domain}/urls` | https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trellocm/urls |
| **Parameters** | `limit`, `after` (for paging), optional filters | `?limit=20&after=tr_cursor1` |

> ⚠️ Replace `trellocm` with the correct domain name exactly as stored in VT (e.g., `trello.com`).

#### 1️⃣ Using cURL

```bash
export XVT_API_KEY="tr_key001"

curl -s \
     --request GET \
     --url "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com/urls?limit=20&after=tr_cursor1" \
     --header "x-apikey: $XVT_API_KEY"
```

This returns JSON similar to:

```json
{
  "data": [
    { "id": "...", "attributes": {...}, ... },
    ...
  ],
  "links": {
      "next": "/api/v3/...?...",
      "prev": null,
      "self": "/api/v3/...?"
  }
}
```

Take note of the `"next"` link—if you hit the end of the page, you'll see another cursor there.

#### 2️⃣ Using Python Requests

```python
import os
import requests

API_KEY   = os.getenv("XVT_API_KEY") or "tr_key001"
BASE_URL  = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3"
DOMAIN    = "trello.com"
CURSOR    = "tr_cursor1"          # start point
LIMIT     = 20                    # max per request

headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

params = {
    "limit": LIMIT,
    "after": CURSOR            # <-- pagination token
}

resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/domains/{DOMAIN}/urls",
                    headers=headers,
                    params=params)

print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.json())
```

If you’d like to iterate over all pages until you’ve collected 20 unique URLs, wrap the above logic inside a loop that updates `CURSOR` with each iteration's `"next"` link.

---

### Things to Keep In Mind

| Topic | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Rate Limits** | Free tier → ~4 requests/minute. Paid tiers allow higher throughput. |
| **Cursor vs Offset** | VT uses opaque cursors (`after=`). Don’t try to guess numeric offsets. |
| **Data Fields** | Each URL object contains fields like `last_analysis_stats`, `first_submission_date`, `tags`, etc. Filter them client‑side if needed. |
| **Error Handling** | A non‑200 status may mean “invalid cursor” or “rate limit exceeded.” Check `error.code`. |
| **Pagination** | If fewer than 20 items remain after your last cursor, the returned array will simply contain whatever remains. No extra padding. |

---

### Sample Output Skeleton

Below is what you’ll typically receive when pulling 20 URLs:

```json
{
  "meta": {
    "page_size": 20,
    "total_count": 12345
  },
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "http://example.trello.com/some/path",
      "attributes": {
        "category": ["malicious"],
        "reputation_score": 0.9,
        "submission_time": "2025-04-01T12:34:56Z",
        "analyses": {
           "positive": 10,
           "negative": 90,
           "undetected": 100
        }
      }
    },
    /* …19 more objects… */
  ]
}
```

Feel free to tweak the parameters (`limit`, `filter[...]=value`) to narrow down the result set further—for instance, only URLs flagged as malicious, or only those submitted in the past week.

---

Let me know if you'd like help parsing the output into CSV, filtering specific attributes, or automating repeated queries!
